newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TRANSFERS 32.9 PCT OF PBR TO PBK.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TRANSFERS 32.9 PCT OF PBR TO PBK.

text.p: The Polish state treasury transferred 32.9 percent of its shares in Polish Development Bank SA (PBR) to state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), PBR said in a statement on Tuesday.
The bank said the treasury cut its stake to 29.54 percent from the earlier 62.48 percent.
The statement said the treasury move was aimed at increasing PBK's share capital.

It said that after the move PBK would become PBR's main shareholder. Other large stockholders as of May 1996, are the government's Industry Development Agency (IDA) with a 16.3 percent stake and Citibank Poland SA with a 7.3 percent stake.
PBK, slated for sale to a strategic investor or a consortium early next year, has signalled its interest in taking about 30 percent of PBR's shares.

The bank, which has agreed on a cross-shareholding plan with the listed Kredyt Bank SA said in June it might form a financial group by entering a similar cross-shareholding with PBR. Neither the treasury nor banks would immediately comment on the transaction.
